idiom_name: hand-written struct over a map with a []Call journal guarded by sync.Mutex
implementation_notes: Go interfaces are satisfied implicitly, so the recording fake is an ordinary struct: methods update a map and append a named struct type to a []Call slice, with a sync.Mutex guarding both whenever tests run with t.Parallel() or the system under test starts goroutines; nothing of the classic double structure has to be built, and this hand-written form is the community's standard test double. testify's mock.Mock records calls through On() and Called() and verifies them with AssertCalled or AssertExpectations, but it returns programmed values rather than implementing behaviour, so it serves the mock row. Add a compile-time assertion such as var _ Ledger = (*fakeLedger)(nil) so interface drift breaks the build, and expose the journal through a method that returns a copy.
pitfalls: A fake stored in a package-level variable or built in TestMain shares its map and journal across tests - construct it inside each test.
Appending to the calls slice from concurrent calls without the mutex is a data race that may only surface under -race.
Returning the calls slice directly lets callers append into the fake's backing array; return a copy or a length-bounded sub-slice.
